name: Impressionism
description: Loose brushwork and natural light capturing fleeting moments over academic precision.

name: Post-Impressionism
description: Pushed Impressionism toward personal expression, structure, and symbolic color.

name: Pointillism
description: Color built from tiny dots of pure pigment that blend in the viewer's eye.

name: Symbolism
description: Dreams, myth, and the occult rendered with obsessive craft as a rebuke to rationalism.

name: Art Nouveau
description: Organic curves and botanical forms applied to architecture, posters, and decorative objects.

name: Japanese Woodblock
description: Flat color, bold outline, and radical cropping — a visual grammar that rewired Western modernism.

name: Fauvism
description: Color at maximum intensity, divorced from representation — pure emotional voltage.

name: Expressionism
description: Distorted forms and raw color externalizing inner anguish in an industrializing world.

name: Die Brücke
description: Dresden collective building a bridge to a raw, unmediated future through woodcut and savage color.

name: Cubism
description: Multiple viewpoints collapsed into a single plane — space and time made visible simultaneously.

name: Futurism
description: Speed, machines, and violence celebrated as the aesthetic of the modern age.

name: Vorticism
description: British answer to Futurism — machines and modernity rendered in jagged geometric energy.

name: Constructivism
description: Art built for the revolution: geometric abstraction as a tool for building a new society.

name: Suprematism
description: Pure geometric abstraction stripped of all reference — the black square as zero-point of painting.

name: De Stijl
description: Primary colors, right angles, and horizontal/vertical lines as a universal visual language.

name: Bauhaus
description: Art, craft, and industry merged in a school that shaped how we think about designed objects.

name: Dada
description: Anti-art as protest — nonsense, collage, and readymades as weapons against a civilization that produced WWI.

name: Surrealism
description: The unconscious made visible — dreams, desire, and the irrational erupting into painted reality.

name: Social Realism
description: Labor, poverty, and class struggle depicted with unflinching directness as political act.

name: Muralism
description: Monumental public paintings turning walls into sites of political and indigenous history.

name: Abstract Expressionism
description: Paint as pure feeling — gesture, scale, and raw material over representation or narrative.

name: Color Field
description: Large expanses of flat color creating meditative, immersive fields of pure sensation.

name: CoBrA
description: Spontaneous, childlike imagery from Copenhagen, Brussels, and Amsterdam against cold rationalism.

name: Art Informel
description: European variant of gestural abstraction — tachisme and lyrical mark-making over composition.

name: Pop Art
description: Consumer culture, advertising, and mass media turned into high art with a straight face and a smirk.

name: Minimalism
description: Reduce to the irreducible — industrial materials and geometric forms with no gesture, no narrative, no metaphor.

name: Fluxus
description: Art as event, instruction, or mail — dismantling the boundary between art and everyday life.

name: Conceptual Art
description: The idea is the work — the physical object is optional, documentation is sufficient.

name: Land Art
description: Earth, rock, and landscape as medium — art that cannot be bought, only experienced in place.

name: Arte Povera
description: Humble, raw materials — soil, rags, twigs, coal — used to challenge art's commodification.

name: Process Art
description: The act of making — entropy, gravity, chance — is the subject, not the finished object.

name: Mono-ha
description: Natural and industrial materials placed in relation — stone meets glass meets rope — to reveal encounter over expression.

name: Supports/Surfaces
description: French group interrogating painting's physical components — canvas, stretcher, wall — as the real subject.

name: Institutional Critique
description: Art that turns the gallery, museum, and art market itself into the subject of investigation.

name: Performance Art
description: The body as medium — actions, durational events, and presence as the irreducible artwork.

name: Body Art
description: The artist's own body as site — pain, endurance, transformation, and vulnerability as material.

name: Feminist Art
description: Art that re-centers women's experience, reclaims the domestic, and dismantles the male gaze.

name: Neo-Expressionism
description: Return to figuration and raw painterly gesture as a rebuke of Minimalism's coolness.

name: Transavanguardia
description: Italian Neo-Expressionism — nomadic, mythological imagery reclaiming painting after Conceptualism.

name: Appropriation Art
description: Existing images taken wholesale and re-presented — authorship, originality, and ownership made unstable.

name: New Media Art
description: Video, computers, and networks as artistic material — technology's culture examined from within.

name: Video Art
description: The moving image freed from broadcast — time, repetition, and electronic signal as artistic substance.

name: Street Art
description: Public walls as canvas — graffiti, paste-ups, and murals reclaiming urban space outside the gallery.

name: Identity Art
description: Race, gender, sexuality, and nationality examined through autobiographical and political imagery.

name: Installation Art
description: Entire spaces transformed — the viewer enters and inhabits the work rather than standing before it.

name: Site-Specific Art
description: Work made for and inseparable from a particular place — remove it and you destroy it.

name: Social Practice
description: Art as community, collaboration, and process — participation replaces the contemplated object.

name: Relational Aesthetics
description: Art as social encounter — works create temporary communities, shared meals, and human exchanges.

name: Net Art
description: The internet as medium and subject — browser as canvas, hyperlink as form, network as material.

name: Afrofuturism
description: Science fiction, technology, and African diaspora heritage combined to imagine liberated futures.

name: Superflat
description: Anime, manga, and consumer culture compressed into a deliberately two-dimensional aesthetic.

name: Fiber Art
description: Thread, textile, and weaving recast as fine art — the domestic and the monumental collapsed together.

name: Sound Art
description: Acoustic phenomena as primary artistic material — hearing rather than seeing as the act of viewing.

name: Bioart
description: Living organisms — bacteria, cells, tissue — as medium, raising questions about life, ethics, and manipulation.

name: Post-Internet
description: Art made after the internet is ambient — image circulation, meme culture, and screen aesthetics as subject.

name: New Leipzig School
description: Figurative painting from post-reunification East Germany — psychologically charged, technically rigorous.

name: Zombie Formalism
description: Market-driven abstraction — technically proficient, emotionally empty, optimized for the auction house.

name: Metamodernism
description: Oscillation between modernist sincerity and postmodern irony — earnestness reclaimed without naivety.

name: AI Art
description: Machine learning as collaborator, tool, or subject — authorship and creativity made genuinely uncertain.

name: Generative Art
description: Systems, code, or rules that generate the work — the artist designs the process, not the outcome.

name: Immersive Art
description: Total environmental experience — light, sound, and projection enveloping the viewer's entire body.

name: Postcolonial Art
description: Art interrogating and recovering from colonial histories — voice, representation, and cultural sovereignty.
